questions.q: In the example diary, 30 of 100 days were *Sunny & Walk* and 45 days were *Sunny* in total. What is $P(\text{Walk} \mid \text{Sunny})$?
questions.explain: Conditioning keeps only the Sunny row and re-normalizes it: $P(y\mid x) = P(x,y)/P(x) = 0.30/0.45 \approx 0.667$. $0.30$ is the *joint* probability, and $0.135 = 0.30 \times 0.45$ multiplies instead of dividing.

questions.q: Pressing **Make independent** replaces every cell by $P(x)\,P(y)$ (the outer product of the marginals). What stays exactly the same?
options: Nothing — the total number of days changes
questions.explain: Row and column sums of $P(x)P(y)$ are $P(x)\sum_y P(y) = P(x)$ and $P(y)$, so the margins are preserved. The cells and the conditionals change (every conditional row becomes $P(Y)$). Two tables can share margins yet differ in dependence.

questions.q: A bivariate Gaussian has $\mu_x = \mu_y = 0$, $\sigma_x = 1$, $\sigma_y = 2$, $\rho = 0.5$. What is $\mathbb{E}[X \mid Y = 2]$?
options: $0$, because the marginal mean of $X$ is $0$
questions.explain: $\mathbb{E}[X\mid y_0] = \mu_x + \rho\frac{\sigma_x}{\sigma_y}(y_0-\mu_y) = 0 + 0.5 \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot 2 = 0.5$. Forgetting the ratio $\sigma_x/\sigma_y$ gives $1.0$; $0$ ignores the correlation.

questions.q: With $\sigma_x = 1$ and $\sigma_y = 1$, someone proposes $\sigma_{xy} = \text{Cov}(X,Y) = 1.5$. Why does the page reject this $\Sigma$?
options: $\det\Sigma = 1 - 1.5^2 < 0$, so $\Sigma$ has a negative eigenvalue — it is not positive semi-definite (equivalently $|\rho| > 1$)
Nothing is wrong; the contours just become more elongated
questions.explain: A covariance matrix must be PSD: here that means $|\sigma_{xy}| \le \sigma_x\sigma_y = 1$, i.e. $|\rho| \le 1$. Negative covariances are perfectly valid, and the matrix is symmetric by construction.
